A square vanishes at one abscissa only, namely the axis $x=5$. The level $y=-4$ is the vertex height itself, so the line touches the graph once instead of cutting it twice.

There is only one meeting.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.73.context: Consider the quadratic $q(x)=x^{2}-10x+21$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.73.solution_overview:
Alles Folgende bezieht sich auf dieselbe Parabel.

$$q(x)=x^{2}-10x+21$$

Bevor du irgendetwas prüfst, lohnt es sich, den Scheitel sowie Summe und Produkt der Wurzeln aufzuschreiben — alles drei ist Koeffizientenrechnung.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(5,-4\right),\qquad S = 10,\qquad P = 21
$$

Because the discriminant is positive the parabola meets the $x$-axis in two points, and factoring recovers them.

$$
\Delta = 16,\qquad x_{1} = 3,\qquad x_{2} = 7
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-4$.

MATH 7.74.title: Kraftstoffverbrauch gegen Reisegeschwindigkeit
statements: The fuel use is smallest at $x=50$.
The smallest possible fuel use equals $30$ litres.
Zwischen $x=20$ und $x=40$ ändert sich der Kraftstoffverbrauch mit der mittleren Rate von $-1$ Litern pro Einheit von $x$.
The fuel use is never zero.
At $x=100$ the fuel use equals $80$ litres.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Fuel use follows a parabola, so the most economical speed is the abscissa of the Extrempunkt, read from the first two coefficients.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

$$a=\frac{1}{50},\ b$$

$$a=-2$$

$$x=-\frac{-2}{2\cdot\frac{1}{50}}$$

$$x=50$$

The Leitkoeffizient $\frac{1}{50}$ is positive, so the model falls to that input and rises afterwards.

The fuel use is smallest at $x=50$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The extreme fuel use is the height of the Extrempunkt, so evaluate the model at $x=50$.

$$F(50)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 50^{2}-2\cdot 50+80$$

$$50^{2}=2500$$

$$F(50)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 2500-2\cdot 50+80$$

$$F(50)=50^{2}-100+80$$

$$50^{2}=2500$$

$$F(50)=50-100+80$$

$$F(50)=50-100$$

$$F(50)=-50$$

$$F(50)=-50+80$$

$$F(50)=30$$

Because $a=\frac{1}{50}>0$ this height is the smallest value the model ever reaches.

The smallest fuel use is $30$ litres.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

An average rate compares the change of fuel use with the change of speed, so evaluate both endpoints first and then divide.

$$F(20)=\frac{400}{50}-40+80$$

$$F(20)=48$$

$$F(40)=\frac{1600}{50}-80+80$$

$$F(40)=32$$

$$\frac{F(40)-F(20)}{40-20}=\frac{-16}{20}$$

$$\frac{F(40)-F(20)}{40-20}=-\frac{4}{5}$$

The average rate over that stretch is $-\frac{4}{5}$, not the claimed $-1$.

The claimed rate $-1$ is wrong.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

Fuel use hits zero exactly when the quadratic has a real root, so compute the discriminant.

$$\Delta=(-2)^{2}-4\cdot\frac{1}{50}\cdot 80$$

$$\Delta=4-\frac{16}{5}$$

$$\Delta=-\frac{12}{5}$$

A negative discriminant keeps the whole graph on one side of the horizontal axis. The vertex height $30$ already sits strictly above zero.

$$F(50)=30$$

$$30>0$$

The model never returns a zero fuel use.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

Substitute the cruising speed $100$ into the model and simplify term by term.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

$$F(100)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 100^{2}-2\cdot 100+80$$

$$100^{2}=10000$$

$$F(100)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 10000-2\cdot 100+80$$

$$F(100)=200-200+80$$

$$F(100)=200-200$$

$$F(100)=0$$

$$F(100)=0+80$$

$$F(100)=80$$

The square term and the linear term cancel, leaving the constant $80$.

The fuel use at $x=100$ is $80$ litres.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.74.context: For a lorry cruising at $x$ kilometres per hour, the fuel used on a fixed route is modelled by $F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$ litres. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.74.solution_overview:
The story reduces to one formula and the quantities it links.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

The completed square hands over the Extrempunkt, and Vieta's relations hand over the sum and the product of the roots.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(50,30\right),\qquad S = 100,\qquad P = 4000
$$

A negative discriminant keeps the graph entirely on one side of the $x$-axis.

$$\Delta=-\frac{12}{5}$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $30$.

MATH 7.75.title: Eine Parabel durch Scheitel und einen Punkt festgelegt
statements: The rule is $q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$.
Die Wurzeln von $q$ sind $1$ und $5$.
Der Graph von $q$ trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=10$.
Der Leitkoeffizient von $q$ ist $2$.
The horizontal line $y=-8$ meets the graph of $q$ at two different points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A vertex already fixes the shape up to one stretch factor, so write the parabola in completed-square form and let the extra point decide the factor.

$$q(x)=a(x-3)^{2}-8$$

Substituting the point $(1,0)$ leaves one equation for $a$.

$$0 = a(1-3)^{2}-8$$

$$a$$

$$q(x)=2$$

Expanding the square puts the rule in standard form.

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

The rebuilt rule is the one printed in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

One root is already handed over as the extra point $(1,0)$. The axis is $x=3$, so the other root is the mirror of $1$ in that axis.

$$3-(1-3)=5$$

Checking against the rebuilt formula $q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$: expanding gives

$$2x^{2}-12x+10=2(x-1)(x-5)$$

$$x=1$$

$$x=5$$

Die Nullstellen sind $1$ und $5$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The vertical intercept is the value at $x=0$ of the completed-square form with the stretch $a=2$ forced by the extra point.

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(0)=2\cdot 9-8$$

$$q(0)=10$$

That is also the constant term of $2x^{2}-12x+10$.

Der Graph trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=10$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The stretch $a$ was forced by the extra point $(1,0)$. Substitute into the Scheitelpunktform.

$$q(x)=a(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$0=a\cdot(1-3)^{2}-8$$

$$0=4a-8$$

$$a=2$$

Expand to confirm the Leitkoeffizient:

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

The number multiplying $x^{2}$ is $2$. The Leitkoeffizient is $2$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The horizontal line $y=-8$ is the vertex height itself, so meetings solve $q(x)+8=0$.

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(x)+8=2(x-3)^{2}$$

A square times $2$ vanishes at one abscissa only:

$$x=3$$

The line touches the graph once at the vertex instead of cutting it twice. There is only one meeting.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.75.context: A parabola $q$ has its vertex at $(3,-8)$ and passes through the point $(1,0)$; recover its rule before judging the claims. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.75.solution_overview:
A vertex already fixes the shape up to one stretch factor, so write the parabola in completed-square form and let the extra point decide the factor.

$$q(x)=a\left(x-3\right)^{2}-8$$

Substituting the point $(1,0)$ leaves one equation for $a$.

$$
0 = a\left(1-3\right)^{2}-8\Rightarrow a = 2
$$

Expanding the square puts the rule in standard form.

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

Completing the square locates the Extrempunkt, and Vieta's relations give the sum $S$ and the product $P$ of the roots without solving anything.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(3,-8\right),\qquad S = 6,\qquad P = 5
$$

Die Diskriminante ist positiv, daher schneidet der Graph die $x$-Achse zweimal — je einmal links und rechts der Symmetrieachse.

$$
\Delta = 64,\qquad x_{1} = 1,\qquad x_{2} = 5
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

MATH 7.76.title: Eine Gewinnkurve mit zwei Break-even-Punkten
statements: The profit is largest at $x=12$.
The largest possible profit equals $64$.
Der Gewinn ist genau bei $x=4$ und $x=20$ null.
Zwischen $x=0$ und $x=10$ ändert sich der Gewinn mit der mittleren Rate von $14$ pro Einheit von $x$.
At $x=2$ the profit equals $0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Profit follows a parabola, so the best output is the abscissa of the Extrempunkt, read from the first two coefficients.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

$$a=-1,\ b$$

$$a=24$$

$$x=-\frac{24}{2\cdot(-1)}$$

$$x=12$$

The Leitkoeffizient $-1$ is negative, so the model rises up to that input and falls afterwards.

The profit is largest at $x=12$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The extreme profit is the height of the Extrempunkt of $P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$, so evaluate the model at the axis $x=12$.

$$P(12)=-12^{2}+24\cdot 12-80$$

$$12^{2}=144$$

$$P(12)=-144+24\cdot 12-80$$

$$P(12)=64$$

$$P(12)=-144+288-80$$

Because $a=-1<0$ this height is the largest value the model ever reaches; the arms fall on both sides.

The largest profit is $64$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Profit is zero at the roots of the quadratic, so multiply by $-1$ and factor the resulting monic polynomial.

$$-x^{2}+24x-80 = 0$$

$$x^{2}-24x+80 = 0$$

$$(x-4)(x-20)=0$$

$$x=4$$

$$x=20$$

Those are the two break-even levels named in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

An average rate compares the change of profit with the change of output, so evaluate both endpoints first and then divide.

$$P(0)=-80$$

$$P(10)=-100+240-80$$

$$P(10)=-100+240$$

$$P(10)=140$$

$$P(10)=140-80$$

$$P(10)=60$$

$$\frac{P(10)-P(0)}{10-0}=\frac{140}{10}$$

$$\frac{P(10)-P(0)}{10-0}=14$$

The average rate over that stretch is $14$.

The average rate is $14$ per unit of $x$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The claim that two machines already break even is a substitution into the profit model.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

$$P(2)=-4+48-80$$

$$P(2)=-4+48$$

$$P(2)=44$$

$$P(2)=44-80$$

$$P(2)=-36$$

The true zeros sit at $x=4$ and $x=20$, so $x=2$ is still on the loss side of the first break-even.

The profit is $-36$, not $0$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.76.context: A workshop's monthly profit in hundreds of euros, when $x$ machines are produced, is modelled by $P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.76.solution_overview:
The situation is captured by a single rule.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

Two standard readings cover most of what follows: the vertex from the completed square, and the sum and product of the roots from the coefficients.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(12,64\right),\qquad S = 24,\qquad P = 80
$$

Two real roots follow from the positive discriminant, and the Symmetrieachse sits exactly halfway between them.

$$
\Delta = 256,\qquad x_{1} = 4,\qquad x_{2} = 20
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach unten, daher ist der Extrempunkt der höchste Punkt des Graphen und der größte Wert ist $64$.

MATH 7.77.title: Halbskalierte Faktoren und die Werte einer Parabel
statements: Die Wurzeln von $w$ sind $-1$ und $7$.
Die Symmetrieachse von $w$ ist die Gerade $x=3$.
Expanding gives $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$.
Der kleinste von $w$ angenommene Wert ist $-8$.
$w(x)\ge 0$ holds for every real $x$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A product vanishes exactly when one of its factors does, and the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ never vanishes, so the brackets already display the roots.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+1)(x-7)$$

$$w(x)=0$$

$$x=-1$$

$$x=7$$

No expanding is required, and there are no other zeros.

Die Wurzeln sind $-1$ und $7$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The axis sits halfway between the two roots named by the brackets; the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ does not move that midpoint.

$$x=\frac{-1+7}{2}$$

$$x=\frac{6}{2}$$

$$x=3$$

Expanding and using $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ recovers the same line: $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$ gives

$$x=-\frac{-3}{2\cdot\frac{1}{2}}$$

Die Achse ist $x=3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Multiply the two brackets out and then apply the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$; the function itself does not change.

$$(x+1)(x-7)=x^{2}-6x-7$$

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$$

Every coefficient agrees with the displayed expansion.

The expanded rule is $\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The smallest value is the height on the axis $x=3$, because the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ is positive.

$$w(3)=\frac{1}{2}(3+1)(3-7)$$

$$w(3)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot(-4)$$

$$w(3)=-8$$

The arms rise on both sides, so $-8$ is the smallest value and there is no largest one.

Der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Eine Ungleichung, die für jedes reelle $x$ gelten muss, ist eine Aussage über die Scheitelhöhe. Die Streckung $\frac{1}{2}$ ist positiv, daher fallen die Werte nie unter den Scheitel, aber zwischen den beiden Wurzeln fallen sie unter $0$.

$$w(3)=-8$$

$$w(x)\ge -8\qquad w(3)=-8$$

$$-8<0$$

The claimed bound $0$ is broken at the Extrempunkt.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.77.context: Consider $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(x+1\right)\left(x-7\right)$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.77.solution_overview:
There is one graph to study, and it is a parabola.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(x+1\right)\left(x-7\right)$$

Ausmultiplizieren bringt dieselbe Vorschrift in die Standardform, in der jeder Koeffizient direkt abgelesen werden kann.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$$

Die Achsenformel legt den Extrempunkt fest, während Summe $S$ und Produkt $P$ der Wurzeln ohne zu lösende Gleichung aus den Koeffizienten folgen.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(3,-8\right),\qquad S = 6,\qquad P = -7
$$

Because the discriminant is positive the parabola meets the $x$-axis in two points, and factoring recovers them.

$$
\Delta = 16,\qquad x_{1} = -1,\qquad x_{2} = 7
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

MATH 7.78.title: Höhen eines Steins, jede Sekunde erfasst
statements: Die ersten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant.
Die zweiten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant und gleich $-10$.
Die Tabelle wird durch die Vorschrift $y=-5x^{2}+30x$ erzeugt.
The $y$-values in the table are largest at $x=3$.
Continuing the pattern, the value at $x=5$ is $25$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Falsch

List the five heights from the table and subtract neighbours; constant first differences would be the fingerprint of a line.

$$y:\ 0,\ 25,\ 40,\ 45,\ 40$$

$$\text{first differences}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5$$

The steps come in four different sizes, and they even change sign after the peak.

The first differences are not constant.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**B.** → Wahr

Differencing the first differences once more produces the second differences, which for a quadratic rule are constant.

$$\text{first differences}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5$$

$$\text{second differences}:\ -10,\ -10,\ -10$$

They are all equal to $-10$, the value the claim names.

The second differences are constant and equal to $-10$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Substitute the claimed rule into the listed seconds; for a quadratic, matching three rows already pins the rule down, and the remaining two are a check.

$$y=-5x^{2}+30x$$

$$0\mapsto 0,\quad 1\mapsto 25,\quad 2\mapsto 40,\quad 3\mapsto 45,\quad 4\mapsto 40$$

Every row of the table is reproduced.

Die Tabelle wird durch $y=-5x^{2}+30x$ erzeugt.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Compare the five listed heights and see where the largest one sits; the claim is about the table itself, not about a continuous model.

$$y:\ 0,\ 25,\ 40,\ 45,\ 40$$

The largest listed value is $45$, and it appears at $x=3$. The neighbouring values $40$ and $40$ are both smaller.

The $y$-values in the table are largest at $x=3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The next first-difference shrinks by the constant second difference $-10$, so add $-5+(-10)=-15$ to the last height $40$.

$$40+(-15)=25$$

The same height comes from the quadratic rule already identified.

$$y(5)=-5\cdot 25+150$$

$$y(5)=25$$

The value at $x=5$ is $25$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.78.context: A stone is launched upwards and its height above the ground is measured once per second. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.78.solution_overview:
Die Tabelle ist der gesamte Aufgabentext; lies sie als Liste von Paaren.

$$\left(0,0\right),\ \left(1,25\right),\ \left(2,40\right),\ \left(3,45\right),\ \left(4,40\right)$$

Die Eingaben sind gleichabständig, daher sind die Differenzen benachbarter Ausgaben das schnellste Diagnosewerkzeug.

$$\text{first}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5\qquad \text{second}:\ -10,\ -10,\ -10$$

The first differences move while the second ones stand still, the signature of a parabola; the constant second difference is twice the Leitkoeffizient times the squared spacing.

$$y=-5x^{2}+30x$$

MATH 7.79.title: Eine Gerade um eine Parabel rückgängig machen
statements: The inverse $f^{-1}$ is again a non-constant linear function.
The nested function $g(f^{-1}(x))$ is a quadratic function.
The nested function $f^{-1}(g(x))$ is a quadratic function.
The nested function $g(f^{-1}(x))$ always has the same roots as $g$.
The nested function $f^{-1}(g(x))$ always has the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ with $m\neq 0$ and undo it by solving $y=mx+q$ for $x$.

$$y = mx+q$$

$$x = \frac{y-q}{m}$$

The division is legitimate precisely because the line is non-constant, and the result is again a first-degree formula.

$$f^{-1}(y)=\frac{1}{m}y-\frac{q}{m}$$

Its slope is $1/m$, which is a non-zero number, so the inverse is not a constant function.

Undoing a non-constant line gives another non-constant line.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Nesting the inverse line inside the parabola substitutes a first-degree expression for $x$, so expand the square and collect the terms.

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=a\left(\frac{x-q}{m}\right)^{2}+b\left(\frac{x-q}{m}\right)+c$$

The square of a first-degree expression reaches $x^{2}$ and stops there, and the coefficient it produces is the leading one of the composite.

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{2}=\frac{a}{m^{2}}\neq 0$$

It is non-zero because $a\neq 0$ and $m\neq 0$, so nothing cancels the square term.

The composite is again a parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

In this order the parabola is computed first and the inverse line is applied afterwards, which merely rescales and shifts the values.

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{g(x)-q}{m}$$

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{a}{m}x^{2}+\frac{b}{m}x+\frac{c-q}{m}$$

The Leitkoeffizient $a/m$ is again non-zero, so the square term survives the rescaling.

The composite is a parabola in this order as well.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

Here the inverse line acts on the argument, so a root of the composite is an abscissa whose image under $f^{-1}$ is a root of $g$; the roots get moved rather than kept.

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=0$$

$$f^{-1}(x)\text{ is a root of }g$$

Take the simplest concrete pair and follow the bookkeeping.

$$g(x)=x^{2}$$

$$f(x)=x+1$$

$$S=f^{-1}(x)$$

$$S=x-1$$

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=\left(x-1\right)^{2}$$

The composite vanishes at $x=1$ while $g$ vanishes at $x=0$, so the two root sets are different.

Substituting inside the parabola shifts its roots.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

In this order the line acts after the parabola, and an operation performed on the values can only stretch or slide the graph vertically.

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{a}{m}x^{2}+\frac{b}{m}x+\frac{c-q}{m}$$

Both the leading and the middle coefficient are divided by the same non-zero number $m$, so the quotient that produces the axis is unchanged.

$$-\frac{b/m}{2\left(a/m\right)}=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

The composite has exactly the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.79.context: A non-constant line $f$ with inverse $f^{-1}$ is given together with a parabola $g$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.79.solution_overview:
Everything is stated for a general parabola, so the reasoning runs on the structure of $ax^{2}+bx+c$ instead of on numbers.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x-q}{m}
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Das Nesten zweier Polynome multipliziert ihre höchsten Potenzen statt sie zu addieren, daher lässt eine Gerade in einer Parabel weiterhin eine Parabel. Das Umkehren einer Geraden ergibt wieder eine Gerade, daher kann das Einwickeln um eine Parabel die höchste auftretende Potenz nicht ändern.

MATH 7.80.title: Eine Gerade und eine Parabel spiegeln
statements: Die Graphen von $\tilde f$ und $\tilde g$ schneiden sich genau so oft wie die von $f$ und $g$.
Wenn die Graphen von $f$ und $g$ tangential sind, dann auch die von $\tilde f$ und $\tilde g$.
Mirroring in this way can turn two meetings into three.
The parabola $\tilde g$ always opens in the same direction as $g$.
The parabola $\tilde g$ always has the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Mirroring replaces $x$ by $-x$ in both formulas at once, so the equation for the common abscissas is transported by the same substitution.

$$\tilde f(x) = \tilde g(x)$$

$$f(-x) = g(-x)$$

Hence $x$ is a meeting abscissa of the mirrored pair exactly when $-x$ is a meeting abscissa of the original pair.

$$x\text{ solves the new equation}\iff -x\text{ solves the old one}$$

The assignment $x\mapsto -x$ pairs the two sets of solutions one against one, and a reflection can neither create nor destroy a meeting.

The counts agree.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Tangency is the algebraic statement that the difference has a repeated root, so mirror the difference and inspect its shape.

$$\tilde g(x)-\tilde f(x)=(g-f)(-x)$$

If the original graphs are tangent at abscissa $h$, the difference is a perfect square times its Leitkoeffizient.

$$g(x)-f(x) = a(x-h)^{2}$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=(g-f)(-x)$$

$$\tilde g(x)-\tilde f(x)=a(x+h)^{2}$$

The mirrored difference is again a square with the same Leitkoeffizient, now with its repeated root at $-h$.

The reflected graphs touch at the mirrored abscissa.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

Write $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ and $f(x)=mx+q$. The number of meetings is governed by the difference, and mirroring keeps that difference quadratic with the same Leitkoeffizient.

$$(g-f)(-x)=ax^{2}-(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

A quadratic equation has at most two real solutions, so three meetings are out of reach; the correspondence $x\mapsto -x$ shows the count was preserved exactly anyway.

$$a\neq 0$$

$$\text{at most two solutions}$$

Two meetings stay two meetings under a reflection.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The opening direction depends only on the coefficient of $x^{2}$, so mirror the formula $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ and read that coefficient off.

$$\tilde g(x)=a(-x)^{2}+b(-x)+c$$

$$\tilde g(x)=ax^{2}-bx+c$$

Squaring kills the minus sign, so the Leitkoeffizient is still $a$ and its sign has not moved.

The mirrored parabola opens the same way as the original.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Reflecting across the vertical coordinate axis carries the Symmetrieachse along with the graph, so compute where it lands.

$$\tilde g(x) = ax^{2}-bx+c$$

$$\text{axis }x=\frac{b}{2a}$$

The original axis is $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$, so the two lines are opposites of each other and coincide only when $b=0$. A concrete pair makes the jump visible.

$$g(x) = (x-1)^{2}$$

$$\tilde g(x)=(x+1)^{2}$$

In this example the axis jumps from $x=1$ to $x=-1$, two different vertical lines.

The axis is mirrored too, so it generally moves.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.80.context: A line $f$ and a parabola $g$ are mirrored by replacing $x$ with $-x$: write $\tilde f(x)=f(-x)$ and $\tilde g(x)=g(-x)$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.80.solution_overview:
No coefficients are fixed, so the letters $a$, $b$ and $c$ have to be handled through the formulas that hold for every parabola.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad \Delta = b^{2}-4ac
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird. Das Ersetzen von $x$ durch $-x$ spiegelt einen Graphen an der $y$-Achse, und eine Parabel übersteht diesen Tausch genau dann, wenn ihr mittlerer Koeffizient verschwindet.

Both graphs are reflected at once, so the question is always which feature survives a reflection.

MATH 7.81.title: Wie viele Punkte legen eine Kurve fest?
statements: Exactly one linear function has both $P$ and $Q$ on its graph.
There is always at least one quadratic function having $P$, $Q$ and $R$ on its graph.
If $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are not collinear, then exactly one quadratic function has all three on its graph.
Infinitely many quadratic functions have both $P$ and $Q$ on their graphs.
A quadratic function and a linear function can agree at all three points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Two points with different abscissas determine a slope, and the slope together with one of the points determines the whole line.

The denominator is non-zero because $P$ and $Q$ do not lie on a common vertical line, so this quotient is a genuine number; the intercept then has no freedom left.

Any line through both points must have this slope and this intercept, so no second one is possible.

Exactly one linear function passes through the two points.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Three points with distinct abscissas are always matched by exactly one formula of the shape $Ax^{2}+Bx+C$, but nothing guarantees that $A$ comes out non-zero.

$$A x_{P}^{2}+B x_{P}+C=y_{P},\quad\text{and likewise for }Q\text{ and }R$$

If the three points happen to be collinear, that unique solution is the line through them, with a vanishing square coefficient.

$$(0,0),\;(1,1),\;(2,2)$$

$$A=0,\quad B=1,\quad C=0$$

A quadratic function needs a non-zero coefficient of $x^{2}$, so in this configuration there is no quadratic function at all through the three points.

Collinear triples admit only a line, so the existence claim fails in general.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

The three interpolation conditions form a system in the unknown coefficients, and distinct abscissas make it solvable in exactly one way.

$$
A x_{P}^{2}+B x_{P}+C=y_{P},\qquad A x_{Q}^{2}+B x_{Q}+C = y_{Q},\qquad A x_{R}^{2}+B x_{R}+C = y_{R}
$$

Subtracting the equations in pairs eliminates $C$ and then $B$, leaving one value for $A$, after which $B$ and $C$ follow in turn; every step divides only by differences of the abscissas, which are non-zero.

$$A=0$$

$$P,\,Q,\,R\text{ are collinear}$$

Since the points are assumed not to be collinear, the value obtained for $A$ is non-zero and the interpolating formula really is a quadratic one.

There is one such quadratic function and no more.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Passing through two points leaves one degree of freedom, and it can be displayed explicitly: start from the line through $P$ and $Q$ and add a term that vanishes at both abscissas.

$$g_{\lambda}(x)=\lambda(x-x_{P})(x-x_{Q})+mx+q$$

At $x=x_{P}$ and $x=x_{Q}$ the first summand is zero, so every member of this family contains both points, while the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $\lambda$.

$$\lambda\neq 0$$

$$g_{\lambda}\text{ is a quadratic function}$$

Different non-zero values of $\lambda$ give different functions, and there are infinitely many of them.

Infinitely many parabolas pass through the same two points.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Agreement at a point means the difference of the two functions vanishes there, so study that difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)\qquad a\neq 0$$

This is a quadratic expression, so it can vanish at two abscissas at most; three distinct abscissas are one too many.

$$x_{P},\,x_{Q},\,x_{R}\text{ distinct}$$

$$\text{three roots needed}$$

The abscissas are pairwise different because no two of the points share a vertical line, so the required third root cannot exist.

A parabola and a line can agree at two points but never at three.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.81.context: Three pairwise distinct points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ of the plane are given, no two of which lie on the same vertical line. No coordinates are supplied. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.81.solution_overview:
Die Punkte bleiben unbenannt, daher ist die Frage eine des Abzählens von Bedingungen gegen unbekannte Koeffizienten.

$$
f(x) = mx+q,\qquad g(x) = ax^{2}+bx+c,\quad a\neq 0
$$

Zwei Punkte mit verschiedenen Abszissen bestimmen genau eine Gerade, und drei nicht kollineare bestimmen genau eine Parabel.

Die Punkte bleiben anonym, daher können nur Abzählargumente die Behauptungen entscheiden.

MATH 7.82.title: Wo die Differenz ihr Extrem erreicht
statements: Außer $m$ verschwindet, unterscheidet sich die Achse von $d$ von der Achse von $g$.
The axis of $d$ never depends on $m$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $d$ equals $a$.
The function $d$ has a smallest value exactly when $a$ is positive.
Wenn die Graphen von $f$ und $g$ tangential sind, dann liegt der Scheitel von $d$ auf der horizontalen Koordinatenachse.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ and $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$. Subtracting the line leaves the square term alone but shifts the middle coefficient by the slope, and the axis is built from exactly those two numbers.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

$$
\text{axis of }d:\ x=-\frac{b-m}{2a},\qquad \text{axis of }g:\ x = -\frac{b}{2a}
$$

Subtracting one from the other leaves a single term, whose vanishing is controlled by the slope alone.

$$-\frac{b-m}{2a}-\Bigl(-\frac{b}{2a}\Bigr)=\frac{m}{2a}$$

As long as $m\neq 0$ this gap is non-zero, so the two axes are different vertical lines.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

The axis of the difference was just computed, and the slope of the line sits right inside the formula.

$$\text{axis of }d:\ x=-\frac{b}{2a}+\frac{m}{2a}$$

Changing $m$ therefore slides that vertical line, and a concrete pair makes the movement visible.

$$g(x)=x^{2},\ m$$

$$g(x)= 0$$

$$\text{axis }x$$

$$m=2$$

$$\text{axis }x$$

$$m=1$$

Tilting the subtracted line moves the lowest point of the difference sideways.

The axis of $d$ does depend on the slope.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

A line contributes an $x$ term and a constant and nothing else, so the square term of the difference is inherited untouched.

$$d(x)=(ax^{2}+bx+c)-(mx+q)$$

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

Whatever slope and intercept the line has, the number in front of $x^{2}$ is still the Leitkoeffizient of $g$, and it is non-zero.

That coefficient equals $a$ exactly.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Whether a parabola has a smallest value is decided by the direction in which it opens, and the difference opens the same way as $g$.

$$d(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$$

With $a>0$ the square is multiplied by a positive number, so the values never sink below the vertex height $k$, which is actually attained at $x=h$.

$$a>0$$

$$d(x)\ge k$$

$$a<0$$

$$d(x)\le k$$

With $a<0$ the picture is turned over: $k$ becomes the largest value and the arms fall without bound, so no smallest value exists.

A minimum exists precisely in the case $a>0$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

Tangency of the two graphs means the equation $g(x)=f(x)$ has a repeated solution, that is, the difference has a double root.

$$d(x)=g(x)-f(x)$$

$$d(x)=a(x-h)^{2}$$

No constant is left over, so the vertex of $d$ sits at height zero.

$$d(h) = 0$$

$$\text{vertex}$$

$$d(x)=(h,0)$$

A point of height zero lies on the horizontal coordinate axis, and $h$ is the abscissa where the line touches the parabola.

The vertex of the difference lands exactly on that axis.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.82.context: A line $f$ with slope $m$ and a parabola $g$ with nonzero Leitkoeffizient $a$ are given; write $d=g-f$ for their difference. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.82.solution_overview:
Since $a$, $b$ and $c$ are never given numbers, each claim has to survive for every admissible choice of them.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad \Delta = b^{2}-4ac
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird. Die Scheitelpunktform setzt den Extrempunkt bei $(h,k)$, und das Vorzeichen von $a$ entscheidet, ob $k$ der kleinste oder der größte angenommene Wert ist.

MATH 7.83.title: Vorzeichen der Wurzeln aus Summe und Produkt
statements: If $P$ is negative, then the two roots have opposite signs.
Wenn $P$ positiv und $S$ negativ ist, dann sind beide Wurzeln negativ.
Wenn $P$ negativ und $a$ positiv ist, dann nimmt $g$ am Ursprung einen negativen Wert an.
If $P$ is positive, then both roots must be positive.
Wenn $S$ verschwindet, dann sind die Wurzeln entgegengesetzt und die Achse ist die vertikale Koordinatenachse.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $S=x_{1}+x_{2}$ and $P=x_{1}x_{2}$ for the two distinct real roots. The product alone already records their signs.

$$P=x_{1}x_{2}$$

$$P=\frac{c}{a}$$

A product of two real numbers is negative only when the factors have opposite signs, since equal signs give a positive product and a zero factor gives zero.

$$P<0$$

$$x_{1}x_{2}<0$$

$$\text{one root}<0<\text{the other}$$

Geometrically the parabola then crosses the horizontal axis once on each side of the origin.

A negative product forces roots of opposite signs.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The product fixes whether the signs agree, and the sum then decides which sign it is.

$$P>0$$

$$x_{1}\text{ and }x_{2}\text{ have the same sign}$$

Two positive numbers would add up to something positive, so a negative sum rules that case out and only the negative one survives.

$$S<0$$

$$x_{1}+x_{2}<0$$

$$\text{both roots}<0$$

For instance $g(x)=x^{2}+3x+2$ has $P=2>0$ and $S=-3<0$, with roots $-1$ and $-2$.

The two conditions together force both roots to be negative.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The value at the origin is the constant term, and the product of the roots expresses that term through $c=aP$.

$$P = \frac{c}{a}$$

$$c=aP$$

With $a>0$ and $P<0$ the product $aP$ is negative, so the constant term is negative.

$$g(0)=c$$

$$g(0)=aP<0$$

This matches the picture: an upward-opening parabola with one root on each side of the origin must dip below the horizontal axis in between, and the origin lies in that stretch.

The function takes a negative value at the origin.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

A positive product only says the two roots share a sign; it does not say which sign, so one counterexample is enough.

$$g(x)=x^{2}+3x+2$$

$$g(x)=(x+1)(x+2)$$

$$x_{1}=-1$$

$$x_{2}=-2$$

$$P=2$$

$$2>0$$

The roots are distinct and real, the product is positive, yet both roots are negative. The missing extra hypothesis would have been a positive sum.

Positivity of the product leaves the negative case wide open.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

A vanishing sum makes the two roots opposites, and the Symmetrieachse is always the half-sum of the roots.

$$S=x_{1}+x_{2}$$

$$S= 0$$

$$x_{2}$$

$$S=-x_{1}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=\frac{S}{2}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=0$$

The line $x=0$ is the vertical coordinate axis, and the two roots sit symmetrically on either side of it at equal distance.

$$S = 0$$

$$b$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x= 0$$

$$g(x)$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=ax^{2}+c$$

Both halves of the claim hold together.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.83.context: A quadratic $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with nonzero $a$ has two distinct real roots; write $S$ for their sum and $P$ for their product. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.83.solution_overview:
Arithmetic is unavailable here: the coefficients stay symbolic, so the axis formula has to be argued with rather than evaluated.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad S = -\frac{b}{a},\qquad P = \frac{c}{a}
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Vietas Beziehungen machen aus den Koeffizienten Summe und Produkt der Wurzeln, ohne eine Gleichung zu lösen. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird.

MATH 7.84.title: Eine Gerade verschieben, bis sie berührt
statements: Es gibt genau einen Wert von $c$, für den die Gerade die Parabel in einem einzigen Punkt berührt.
When the line passes through the origin, it meets the parabola twice.
For every real $c$ the line meets the parabola.
Alle Geraden der Schar haben dieselbe Steigung.
Whatever $c$ is, the graphs meet at no more than two points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The family slides a line of fixed slope up and down, and touching means $g(x)=f_{c}(x)$ has a repeated solution, so form the difference and watch its discriminant.

$$x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c)=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$$

$$x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c)=0$$

$$\Delta(c)=9+4(5+c)$$

$$\Delta(c)=29+4c$$

This is a first-degree expression in the parameter, so it vanishes for one single value.

$$29+4c = 0$$

$$c$$

$$\Delta(c)=-\frac{29}{4}$$

Exactly one member of the family touches the parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Passing through the origin fixes the parameter, since the intercept of $f_{c}$ is $c$ itself.

$$f_{c}(0)=c$$

$$f_{c}(0)= 0$$

$$f_{0}(x)$$

$$f_{c}(0)=x$$

Now count the solutions of the difference at that parameter value.

$$\Delta(0)=29$$

$$29>0$$

A positive discriminant makes the square root a genuine positive number, so the two abscissas $\frac{3\pm\sqrt{29}}{2}$ are real and different.

The line through the origin cuts the parabola twice.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

Whether a member meets the parabola is decided by the sign of the same discriminant, now read as a function of the shift.

$$\Delta(c)=29+4c$$

$$c<-\frac{29}{4}$$

$$\Delta(c)<0$$

Taking $c=-10$, for instance, gives a negative value

$$\Delta(c)=\Delta(-10)$$

$$\Delta(c)=29-40$$

$$\Delta(c)=-11$$

$$-11<0$$

With no real solution left the line has slid too far down and shares no point with the curve.

Sufficiently low members of the family miss the parabola entirely.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The parameter enters $f_{c}$ only as an added constant, so it never touches the coefficient of $x$.

$$f_{c}(x)=x+c$$

$$f_{c}(x_{2})-f_{c}(x_{1})=x_{2}-x_{1}$$

The rate of change is $1$ for every $c$, so all the members are parallel and the whole family is just one line sliding vertically.

Every line of the family has slope one.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The common abscissas are the real roots of the difference, so look at what kind of equation that difference gives.

$$g(x)-f_{c}(x)=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$$

The parameter only shifts the constant term; the coefficient of $x^{2}$ stays $1$ for every $c$, so the equation remains quadratic.

$$\text{leading coefficient}=1\neq 0$$

$$\text{at most two real roots}$$

Depending on the sign of the discriminant the count is two, one or none, but it can never be three.

Two meetings is the maximum, whatever the shift.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.84.context: A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-2x-5$ is compared with the family of slope-one lines $f_c(x)=x+c$, where $c$ runs through $\mathbb{R}$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.84.solution_overview:
A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-2x-5$ is compared with the family of slope-one lines $f_c(x)=x+c$, where $c$ runs through $\mathbb{R}$.

Rekonstruiere hier einmal die gemeinsame Gerade und Parabel; jeder Buchstabe prüft nur die in seiner Behauptung genannte Zusatzrechnung.

$g-f_c=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$ with discriminant $29+4c$: two meetings, one, or none.

$$
x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c) = x^{2}-3x-(5+c) = 0
$$

$$
\Delta(c) = 9+4(5+c) = 29+4c
$$

$$
29+4c = 0\implies c = -\frac{29}{4}
$$

MATH 7.85.title: Den Leitkoeffizienten wählen
statements: Es gibt einen Wert von $a$, für den die Gerade tangential an die Parabel ist.
For every $a\neq 0$ the graphs meet at two distinct points.
Some choice of $a$ makes the graphs miss each other entirely.
Die Symmetrieachse von $g_a$ ist für alle zulässigen $a$ dieselbe.
Jede Parabel der Schar schneidet die $y$-Achse im selben Punkt.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Here the parameter is the Leitkoeffizient itself, so form the difference and treat its discriminant as a function of $a$.

$$ax^{2}+2x-3-(x+1)=ax^{2}+x-4$$

$$ax^{2}+2x-3-(x+1)=0$$

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

Tangency asks for a repeated root, that is a vanishing discriminant, which is a first-degree condition on the parameter.

$$1+16a = 0$$

$$a$$

$$\Delta(a)=-\frac{1}{16}$$

This value is real and non-zero, so it is an admissible member of the family.

One parabola of the family touches the line.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Two distinct meetings require a strictly positive discriminant, so check whether $\Delta(a)=1+16a$ holds for every admissible parameter.

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

$$a<-\frac{1}{16}$$

$$\Delta(a)<0$$

Taking $a=-1$ gives

$$\Delta(a)=\Delta(-1)$$

$$\Delta(a)=1-16$$

$$\Delta(a)=-15$$

$$-15<0$$

so that member has no real meeting abscissa at all.

Sufficiently negative Leitkoeffizients destroy both intersections.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

Missing each other is the case of a negative discriminant, and the discriminant moves along a straight line as the parameter varies.

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

$$1+16a<0$$

$$a<-\frac{1}{16}$$

Any parameter below that threshold works; with $a=-1$ the difference has no real root.

$$-x^{2}+x-4 = 0$$

$$
\Delta=1-16 = -15<0
$$

The corresponding parabola öffnet sich nach unten and stays entirely below the line.

Such a choice of the Leitkoeffizient exists.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The axis of a parabola is computed from its first two coefficients, and here only the leading one carries the parameter $a$.

$$x=-\frac{2}{2a}$$

$$x=-\frac{1}{a}$$

The result depends on $a$, so different members have different axes.

$$a = 1$$

$$x$$

$$x=-1$$

$$a=2$$

$$a=-\frac{1}{2}$$

The axis slides as the Leitkoeffizient changes.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

The crossing with the vertical coordinate axis is the value at $x=0$, and the parameter multiplies $x^{2}$, which vanishes there.

$$g_{a}(0)=a\cdot 0+2\cdot 0-3$$

$$g_{a}(0)=-3$$

So every member of the family reaches the same height at $x=0$, however large or small the Leitkoeffizient is.

$$a = 1$$

$$g_{1}(0)$$

$$g_{a}(0)=-3$$

$$a=-5$$

$$h=g_{-5}(0)$$

$$h=-3$$

The whole family therefore pivots through the single point $(0,-3)$.

All of them cross the $y$-axis at that same point.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.85.context: A one-parameter family of parabolas $g_a(x)=ax^{2}+2x-3$ with $a\neq 0$ is compared with the fixed line $f(x)=x+1$. Consider what the real parameter $a$ can do. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.85.solution_overview:
A one-parameter family of parabolas $g_a(x)=ax^{2}+2x-3$ with $a\neq 0$ is compared with the fixed line $f(x)=x+1$.

Rekonstruiere hier einmal die gemeinsame Gerade und Parabel; jeder Buchstabe prüft nur die in seiner Behauptung genannte Zusatzrechnung.

$g_a-f=ax^{2}+x-4$ with discriminant $1+16a$; all curves pass through $(0,-3)$.

$$
ax^{2}+2x-3-(x+1) = ax^{2}+x-4 = 0
$$

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

$$
1+16a = 0\implies a = -\frac{1}{16}
$$

MATH 7.86.title: Koeffizientenabgleich gegen eine Verknüpfung
statements: Das Anpassen von $g=Af^{2}+Bf+C$ erzwingt $A=\frac{3}{25}$.
Das Anpassen von $g=Af^{2}+Bf+C$ erzwingt $B=-2$.
Die höchste Potenz von $x$ in der verschachtelten Funktion $f(g(x))$ ist $x^{2}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $g=Af^{2}+Bf+C$ with the given line $f(x)=5x+1$. Only the first summand can create an $x^{2}$ term, and squaring the line contributes $25x^{2}$.

$$A\cdot 5^{2}=3$$

$$A=\frac{3}{25}$$

The division is legitimate because the slope $5$ is non-zero, and no other value of $A$ can reproduce the Leitkoeffizient $3$ of $g$.

Matching forces $A=\frac{3}{25}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

With $A=\frac{3}{25}$ already forced by the $x^{2}$ terms, equate the coefficients of $x$ in $A(5x+1)^{2}+B(5x+1)+C$ and in $g(x)=3x^{2}-2x-1$.

$$A(25x^{2}+10x+1)+B(5x+1)+C=3x^{2}-2x-1$$

The coefficient of $x$ on the left is $10A+5B$, and it must equal $-2$.

$$10\cdot\frac{3}{25}+5B = -2$$

$$x=\frac{6}{5}+5B$$

$$x=-2$$

$$B$$

$$A(25x^{2}+10x+1)+B(5x+1)+C=-\frac{16}{25}$$

The forced value is $-\frac{16}{25}$, not the claimed $-2$.

Matching does not force $B=-2$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

Applying the line to the parabola multiplies the parabola by the slope and then adds the intercept, so no new power of $x$ can be created.

$$f\bigl(g(x)\bigr)=5(3x^{2}-2x-1)+1$$

Expanding the bracket keeps the highest power exactly where it was.

$$f\bigl(g(x)\bigr)=15x^{2}-10x-4$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$ with coefficient $15\neq 0$.

The nested function is again a parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

A nested value is computed from the inside outwards: evaluate the inner function at the given number first, then feed the result into the outer function.

$$f(0)=5\cdot 0+1$$

$$f(0)=1$$

That output now becomes the input of $g$.

$$g(1)=3\cdot 1^{2}-2\cdot 1-1$$

$$1^{2}=1$$

$$g(1)=3\cdot 1-2\cdot 1-1$$

$$g(1)=0$$

Der verschachtelte Wert ist $0$.

$g(f(0))=0$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Nesting is not symmetric: feeding the line into the parabola need not agree with feeding the parabola into the line, so each order has to be computed on its own.

$$g(0)=-1$$

$$f(-1)=5\cdot(-1)+1$$

$$f(-1)=-4$$

$$f(0)=1$$

$$g(1)=3-2-1$$

$$g(1)=3-2$$

$$g(1)=1$$

$$g(1)=1-1$$

$$g(1)=0$$

The two orders give $-4$ and $0$, which are different numbers.

$f(g(0))\neq g(f(0))$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.86.context: Lies die Gerade $f(x)=5x+1$ und die Parabel $g(x)=3x^{2}-2x-1$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.86.solution_overview:
Beide Vorschriften sind bereits mit Zahlen gegeben:

$$
f(x) = 5 x + 1,\qquad g(x) = 3 x^{2} - 2 x - 1
$$

Das Umschreiben von $g$ als $a(x-h)^{2}+k$ macht den Scheitel sichtbar, mit $h$ aus der Achsenformel und $k$ durch Einsetzen dieser Abszisse.

$$
g(x) = 3\left(x-\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}-\frac{4}{3},\qquad \text{vertex} = \left(\frac{1}{3},-\frac{4}{3}\right)
$$

Weil $f$ eine Gerade mit von null verschiedener Steigung ist, trägt das Quadrat $f(x)^{2}$ bereits einen $x^{2}$-Term, daher lässt sich $g$ aus $f(x)^{2}$, $f(x)$ und einer Konstanten rekonstruieren. Koeffizientenvergleich liefert

$$
A = \frac{3}{25},\qquad B = -\frac{16}{25},\qquad C = -\frac{12}{25}
$$

MATH 7.87.title: Wurzelabstand gegen die Achse einer Parabel
statements: Der Abstand zwischen den beiden Wurzeln von $p$ ist $13$.
Die Symmetrieachse von $p$ ist die Gerade $x=-\frac{3}{2}$.
The two roots of $p$ add up to $3$.
The two roots of $p$ multiply to $-40$.
$p$ is increasing for every $x>-2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The two roots sit symmetrically on either side of the axis, so their gap is $\sqrt{\Delta}/|a|$. Compute the discriminant of the given parabola first.

$$\Delta=3^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot(-40)$$

$$3^{2}=9$$

$$\Delta=9-4\cdot 1\cdot(-40)$$

$$\Delta=9+160$$

$$\Delta=169$$

$$|x_{1}-x_{2}|=\frac{\sqrt{169}}{1}$$

$$|x_{1}-x_{2}|=13$$

Solving $x^{2}+3x-40=0$ recovers the roots $-8$ and $5$, which are indeed $13$ apart.

The distance between the two roots is $13$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Build the axis from the first two coefficients of the given parabola; the constant $-40$ never enters this formula.

$$p(x)=x^{2}+3x-40$$

$$a=1,\ b$$

$$a=3$$

$$x=-\frac{3}{2\cdot 1}$$

$$x=-\frac{3}{2}$$

The graph is symmetric in that vertical line, which is also the midpoint of the roots $-8$ and $5$.

Die Achse ist $x=-\frac{3}{2}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

The sum of the two roots is minus the middle coefficient divided by the leading one.

$$S=-\frac{b}{a}$$

$$S=-\frac{3}{1}$$

$$S=-3$$

The roots themselves are $-8$ and $5$:

$$S=-8+5$$

The claim reports $3$, which drops the minus sign in $-\frac{b}{a}$. The sum is $-3$, not $3$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The product of the two roots is the constant term divided by the Leitkoeffizient.

$$P=\frac{c}{a}$$

$$P=\frac{-40}{1}$$

$$P=-40$$

Multiplying the roots confirms the value:

$$P=(-8)\cdot 5$$

The claim reports exactly this product. The two roots multiply to $-40$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

A parabola changes direction exactly once, at its axis $x=-\frac{3}{2}$.

$$p(x)=x^{2}+3x-40$$

$$a=1$$

$$1>0$$

With a positive stretch the graph falls on everything to the left of the axis and rises on everything to its right.

The half-line $x>-2$ reaches across the axis $x=-\frac{3}{2}$, where the direction changes: on $-2<x<-\frac{3}{2}$ the function is still decreasing.

The claimed half-line is not entirely on the increasing side.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.87.context: The parabola $p$ is given by $p(x)=x^{2}+3x-40$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.87.solution_overview:
There is one graph to study, and it is a parabola.

$$p(x)=x^{2}+3x-40$$

Die Achsenformel legt den Extrempunkt fest, während Summe $S$ und Produkt $P$ der Wurzeln ohne zu lösende Gleichung aus den Koeffizienten folgen.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(-\frac{3}{2},-\frac{169}{4}\right),\qquad S = -3,\qquad P = -40
$$

Die Diskriminante ist positiv, daher schneidet der Graph die $x$-Achse zweimal — je einmal links und rechts der Symmetrieachse.

$$
\Delta = 169,\qquad x_{1} = -8,\qquad x_{2} = 5
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-\frac{169}{4}$.

MATH 7.88.title: Eine Verschiebung kann eine Parabel nicht abflachen
statements: Quadratische Ergänzung liefert $g(x)=2\left(x+\frac{3}{4}\right)^{2}-\frac{25}{8}$.
Some vertical translation of $g$ makes $f-g$ a constant function.
Der Scheitel des Graphen von $g$ ist $\left(-\frac{3}{4},-\frac{25}{8}\right)$.
Die mittlere Änderungsrate von $g$ auf $[0,2]$ ist gleich der Steigung von $y=f(x)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Completing the square starts from the axis $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ and the height there.

$$g(x)=2x^{2}+3x-2$$

$$x=-\frac{3}{2\cdot 2}$$

$$x=-\frac{3}{4}$$

$$g\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)=2\cdot\tfrac{9}{16}+3\cdot\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)-2$$

$$g\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)=\tfrac{9}{8}-\tfrac{9}{4}-2$$

$$g\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)=-\tfrac{25}{8}$$

Putting the stretch, the shift and the height together recovers the completed square.

$$g(x)=2\bigl(x+\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)^{2}-\tfrac{25}{8}$$

That is the displayed expression.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Translating a graph vertically adds a fixed number to its formula, which changes the constant term and nothing else, so the $x^{2}$ term of the difference survives untouched.

$$f(x)-g(x)=-2x^{2}-9x+6$$

Shifting $g$ by any real $t$ replaces $g$ by $g+t$ in that difference.

$$f(x)-(g(x)+t)=-2x^{2}-9x+(6-t)$$

The coefficient of $x^{2}$ stays $-2$ for every shift $t$, so the difference remains a genuine parabola and never flattens out.

No vertical translation makes $f-g$ constant.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

The Extrempunkt sits on the axis just computed, so its height is the value of $g$ there.

$$x=-\frac{3}{4}$$

$$g\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)=-\tfrac{25}{8}$$

$$\text{vertex}=\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{4},-\tfrac{25}{8}\bigr)$$

The Leitkoeffizient $2$ is positive, so this point is the lowest on the graph.

Der Scheitel ist $\bigl(-\frac{3}{4},-\frac{25}{8}\bigr)$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The average rate of change over an interval is the slope of the chord joining the two endpoint values, so evaluate $g$ at both ends.

$$g(0)=-2$$

$$g(2)=8+6-2$$

$$g(2)=8+6$$

$$g(2)=14$$

$$g(2)=14-2$$

$$g(2)=12$$

$$\frac{g(2)-g(0)}{2-0}=\frac{12-(-2)}{2}$$

$$\frac{g(2)-g(0)}{2-0}=7$$

The line $f(x)=-6x+4$ has slope $-6$, which is a different number.

The chord slope $7$ is not the slope of $f$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

A nested value is computed from the inside outwards: evaluate $g(x)=2x^{2}+3x-2$ at $0$ first, then feed the result into $f(x)=-6x+4$.

$$g(0)=2\cdot 0^{2}+3\cdot 0-2$$

$$0^{2}=0$$

$$g(0)=2\cdot 0+3\cdot 0-2$$

$$g(0)=-2$$

That output now becomes the input of the line.

$$f(-2)=-6\cdot(-2)+4$$

$$f(-2)=12+4$$

$$f(-2)=16$$

Der verschachtelte Wert ist $16$.

$f(g(0))=16$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.88.context: The following pair is given: the line $f(x)=-6x+4$ together with the parabola $g(x)=2x^{2}+3x-2$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.88.solution_overview:
Alles beginnt mit den beiden konkreten Vorschriften

$$
f(x) = 4 - 6 x,\qquad g(x) = 2 x^{2} + 3 x - 2
$$

Steigung, vertikale Achsenabschnitte und Öffnungsrichtung stehen in den Koeffizienten klar da; die Arme gehen nach oben.

$$
m = -6,\qquad f(0) = 4,\qquad g(0) = -2,\qquad a = 2
$$

Quadratische Ergänzung rückt den Extrempunkt der Parabel in den Blick: die Achse kommt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten, und die Höhe ist der Wert von $g$ dort.

$$
g(x) = 2\left(x+\frac{3}{4}\right)^{2}-\frac{25}{8},\qquad \text{vertex} = \left(-\frac{3}{4},-\frac{25}{8}\right)
$$

Der Vergleich der beiden Graphen bedeutet das Lösen von $f(x)=g(x)$, einer quadratischen Gleichung, deren Diskriminante zwei reelle Lösungen meldet.

$$
f(x)-g(x) = - 2 x^{2} - 9 x + 6,\qquad \Delta = 129
$$

MATH 7.89.title: Geraden durch den Scheitel
statements: Wenn $m$ verschwindet, dann ist $V$ der einzige gemeinsame Punkt der beiden Graphen.
If $m$ is nonzero, then the graphs have a second common point different from $V$.
Whatever $m$ is, the two graphs are tangent at $V$.
The two graphs always have at least one common point.
Wenn ein zweiter gemeinsamer Punkt existiert, liegt er genau dann rechts der Achse von $g$, wenn $m$ und $a$ dasselbe Vorzeichen haben.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Put the parabola in Scheitelpunktform around $V=(h,k)$; a line of slope zero through $V$ is simply the horizontal line at that height.

$$g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$$

$$f(x)=k$$

The difference is then a pure square, so the meeting condition has a repeated solution and no other.

$$g(x)-f(x)=a(x-h)^{2}$$

$$g(x)-f(x)= 0$$

$$x$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=h$$

Away from $x=h$ the square is strictly positive and $a\neq 0$, so the difference never returns to zero.

The vertex is the one and only common point in that case.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

A line through the vertex can be written using the same shifted variable, and then the difference factors by hand.

$$f(x)=m(x-h)+k$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=a(x-h)^{2}-m(x-h)$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=(x-h)\bigl(a(x-h)-m\bigr)$$

The first factor gives back the vertex; the second one vanishes at an abscissa obtained by dividing the slope by the Leitkoeffizient.

$$a(x-h) = m$$

$$x$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=h+\frac{m}{a}$$

Because $m\neq 0$ and $a\neq 0$ the shift $m/a$ is non-zero, so this second abscissa really is different from $h$.

A second common point appears as soon as the line is tilted.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

Tangency would mean the factored difference has a repeated root at the vertex, so look at the factorisation once more.

$$g(x)-f(x)=(x-h)\bigl(a(x-h)-m\bigr)$$

For $m\neq 0$ the factor $x-h$ occurs only once, so the difference changes sign at $x=h$ and the graphs cross there instead of touching.

$$g(x)=x^{2},\ f(x)$$

$$g(x)= x$$

$$g(x)=g(x)-f(x)$$

$$g(x)=x(x-1)$$

In this example the line through the vertex $(0,0)$ cuts the parabola again at $x=1$, and near the origin the difference is negative on one side and positive on the other.

Only the horizontal choice $m=0$ produces a genuine tangency.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The line is required to pass through the vertex, so one common point is handed over by the hypothesis itself.

$$f(h)=k$$

$$f(h)=g(h)$$

Both graphs therefore contain the point $V=(h,k)$, whatever the slope $m$ and the Leitkoeffizient $a$ happen to be.

$$g(x)-f(x)=(x-h)\bigl(a(x-h)-m\bigr)$$

Algebraically the factor $x-h$ is always present in the difference, so the meeting can never be lost.

At least the vertex is always shared.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The second meeting was located exactly, so its position relative to the axis $x=h$ is a matter of one sign.

$$x_{2}=h+\frac{m}{a}$$

The point lies to the right of the axis precisely when the added shift is positive, and a quotient of two non-zero numbers is positive exactly when they share a sign.

$$x_{2}>h$$

$$\frac{m}{a}>0$$

$$m\text{ and }a\text{ have the same sign}$$

Opposite signs push the second meeting to the left instead, at the mirrored distance from the axis.

The criterion is exactly the agreement of the two signs.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.89.context: A parabola $g$ has vertex $V$ and nonzero Leitkoeffizient $a$. A line $f$ of slope $m$ is drawn through that same vertex. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.89.solution_overview:
Everything is stated for a general parabola, so the reasoning runs on the structure of $ax^{2}+bx+c$ instead of on numbers.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad \Delta = b^{2}-4ac
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird. Die Scheitelpunktform setzt den Extrempunkt bei $(h,k)$, und das Vorzeichen von $a$ entscheidet, ob $k$ der kleinste oder der größte angenommene Wert ist.

The line is pinned to the vertex $V$, so one common point is there before any computation starts.

MATH 7.90.title: Eine Parabel mit sich selbst verknüpfen
statements: The highest power of $x$ in $g(g(x))$ is $x^{4}$.
The highest power of $x$ in $g(f(g(x)))$ is $x^{4}$.
Die höchste Potenz von $x$ in $g(g(x))$ ist $x^{4}$, weil die beiden Potenzen addiert statt multipliziert werden.
The nested function $f(f(x))$ is again a non-constant linear function.
For a suitable $g$, the nested function $g(g(x))$ is a quadratic function.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Schreibe $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ mit $a\neq 0$. Nesting substitutes the whole parabola in place of $x$, so the square term gets squared and that is where the top power comes from.

$$g\bigl(g(x)\bigr)=a(ax^{2}+bx+c)^{2}+b(ax^{2}+bx+c)+c$$

Squaring an expression whose highest power is $x^{2}$ reaches $x^{4}$, with a coefficient that is a product of non-zero numbers.

$$a(ax^{2})^{2}=a^{3}x^{4}$$

The remaining summands only climb to $x^{2}$, so nothing can cancel the $a^{3}x^{4}$ term.

The highest power really is $x^{4}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Schreibe $f(x)=mx+q$ mit $m\neq 0$. Work from the inside out: applying the line to the parabola only rescales it, and then the outer parabola squares the result.

$$f\bigl(g(x)\bigr)=m(ax^{2}+bx+c)+q$$

The Leitkoeffizient here is $ma$, non-zero because the line is non-constant, so the middle stage is still a parabola.

$$g\bigl(f(g(x))\bigr)=a(ma\,x^{2}+\cdots)^{2}+\cdots$$

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{4}=a(ma)^{2}$$

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{4}= a^{3}m^{2}\neq 0$$

The triple nesting also tops out at $x^{4}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

The value $x^{4}$ is right, but the reason offered is not: powers of nested functions multiply, and here $2$ times $2$ happens to agree with $2$ plus $2$.

$$
2\cdot 2=4,\qquad 2+2 = 4
$$

A single case where the two rules disagree exposes which one is at work: nest the parabola inside the line and count.

$$g\bigl(f(x)\bigr)=a(mx+q)^{2}+b(mx+q)+c$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$, which is $2\cdot 1=2$, not $2+1=3$. Adding the powers is the rule for multiplying two formulas together, not for nesting one inside the other.

The stated justification is the wrong rule, even though the number it produces here is right.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

Schreibe $f(x)=mx+q$ mit $m\neq 0$. Nesting a line inside itself substitutes a first-degree expression into a first-degree formula, so expand and collect.

$$f\bigl(f(x)\bigr)=m(mx+q)+q$$

$$f\bigl(f(x)\bigr)=m^{2}x+q(m+1)$$

The new slope is $m^{2}$, and a square of a non-zero number is non-zero, so the result is a line that is not constant.

$$m\neq 0$$

$$m^{2}>0$$

The double nesting stays a non-constant line.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

For the nesting to collapse to a parabola, the $x^{4}$ term would have to disappear, so look at the coefficient it carries.

$$g\bigl(g(x)\bigr)=a(ax^{2}+bx+c)^{2}+b(ax^{2}+bx+c)+c$$

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{4}=a^{3}$$

This vanishes only when $a=0$, which is forbidden because $g$ is a parabola; no choice of $b$ or $c$ has any influence on it.

$$a\neq 0$$

$$a^{3}\neq 0$$

The $x^{4}$ term is always there, so the nesting is never a quadratic function.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.90.context: A non-constant line $f$ and a parabola $g$ are given. Consider the nested functions $g(g(x))$ and $g(f(g(x)))$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.90.solution_overview:
Es erscheinen keine Zahlen, daher werden die Behauptungen durch das entschieden, was Nesten mit der höchsten Potenz von $x$ macht.

$$
f(x) = mx+q,\qquad g(x) = ax^{2}+bx+c,\quad a\neq 0
$$

Nesten multipliziert die höchsten Potenzen statt sie zu addieren, daher erreicht das Einsetzen einer Parabel in eine Parabel $x^{4}$, und das Einfügen einer Geraden dazwischen ändert daran nichts.

MATH 7.91.title: Kann eine Gerade eine Parabel einschließen?
statements: If $a$ is positive, some line lies strictly below the whole graph of $g$.
If $a$ is positive, some line lies strictly above the whole graph of $g$.
If $a$ is positive, then $g-f$ attains a smallest value for every linear $f$.
If $a$ is negative, some horizontal line lies strictly above the whole graph of $g$.
The graph of $g$ can be squeezed between two distinct parallel lines over all of $\mathbb{R}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

An upward-opening parabola has a lowest point, and any level below that height gives a line the graph never reaches.

$$g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k\ge k\quad\text{for all }x,\qquad a>0$$

Take the horizontal line one unit under the vertex; it is a perfectly legitimate linear function.

$$f(x)=k-1$$

$$g(x)-f(x)\ge 1>0$$

The gap between the two graphs is at least one unit everywhere, so the line stays strictly below the parabola.

Such a line exists, for instance that horizontal one.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

A line above the whole graph would need $g(x)<f(x)$ for every $x$, so examine the difference far from the origin.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q),\quad a>0$$

The difference is itself an upward-opening parabola, so it has a lowest point and then climbs beyond every bound on both sides.

$$g(x)-f(x)>0\text{ for all }|x|\text{ large enough}$$

The arms of the parabola therefore rise past any line eventually, no matter how steep the line is chosen.

No line can stay above the whole graph when $a>0$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

Subtracting a line changes only the $x$ term and the constant term, so the difference keeps the Leitkoeffizient of $g$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q),\quad a>0$$

Completing the square exhibits a non-negative square multiplied by a positive number, plus a constant that is actually attained at the vertex.

$$g(x)-f(x)=a(x-h_{d})^{2}+k_{d}\ge k_{d}$$

The value $k_{d}$ depends on the line chosen, but for each line it is a genuine number reached at one abscissa.

The difference attains a smallest value for every linear $f$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

A negative Leitkoeffizient turns the arms downwards, so the vertex is now the highest point of the graph.

$$g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k\le k\quad\text{for all }x,\qquad a<0$$

The square is non-negative and $a<0$, so the product is at most zero and the values never climb past the vertex height $k$.

$$f(x)=k+1$$

$$f(x)-g(x)\ge 1>0$$

The horizontal line one unit above the vertex therefore misses the graph entirely and stays above it.

Such a horizontal line exists.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

A strip between two parallel lines has bounded width, so being squeezed inside it would keep the difference to one of those lines bounded.

$$f_{1}(x)=mx+q_{1}$$

$$f_{2}(x)=mx+q_{2}$$

Subtracting the lower line from $g$ leaves a parabola with the same Leitkoeffizient $a\neq 0$, and such a difference is unbounded.

$$g(x)-f_{1}(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q_{1})$$

For $a>0$ its values exceed $q_{2}-q_{1}$ once $|x|$ is large, and for $a<0$ they fall below the strip instead, so the graph escapes on one side or the other.

A parabola always breaks out of a strip of finite width.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.91.context: A parabola $g$ with nonzero Leitkoeffizient $a$ is given together with a line $f$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.91.solution_overview:
The parabola arrives already centred on its vertex, so the reasoning stays with the roles of $a$, $h$ and $k$.

$$g(x)=a\left(x-h\right)^{2}+k$$

Die Scheitelpunktform setzt den Extrempunkt bei $(h,k)$, und das Vorzeichen von $a$ entscheidet, ob $k$ der kleinste oder der größte angenommene Wert ist. Weit außen wächst der $x^{2}$-Term jede lineare Terme aus, daher entscheidet die Parabel, wer oben liegt.

MATH 7.92.title: Wurzeln über lineare Substitution lesen
statements: The function $g$ is a quadratic function.
Every real root of $g$ is a point at which $f$ takes a root value of $q$.
If $q$ has no real roots, then $g$ has no real roots.
Die Wurzeln von $g$ stimmen mit den Wurzeln von $q$ überein.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $g$ equals $A$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Schreibe $f(x)=mx+k$ mit $m\neq 0$. Substituting the line into the outer formula replaces $y$ by a first-degree expression, so expand and collect the powers of $x$.

$$g(x)=A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$$

$$g(x)=Am^{2}x^{2}+(2Amk+Bm)x+(Ak^{2}+Bk+C)$$

The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is the product $Am^{2}$, and both factors are non-zero: $A$ by hypothesis and $m$ because the line is non-constant.

The substitution produces a genuine quadratic function.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The composite is evaluated in two stages, so a zero of the whole thing is a zero produced at the second stage.

$$g(x_{0})=q\bigl(f(x_{0})\bigr)$$

If this number is zero then the value $y_{0}=f(x_{0})$ satisfies $q(y_{0})=0$, so it is one of the roots of $q$.

$$g(x_{0}) = 0$$

$$q(y_{0})$$

$$y_{0}=f(x_{0})$$

The reasoning uses nothing but the definition of nesting, so it applies to every real root of $g$.

Each root of the composite is an abscissa where the line hits a root of $q$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The composite can only reach values that $q$ itself takes, so a $q$ that never vanishes hands its property straight over.

$$q(y)\neq 0\text{ for every real }y$$

For any real $x$ the number $f(x)$ is real, so $q$ evaluated there is non-zero as well.

$$g(x)=q\bigl(f(x)\bigr)\neq 0\quad\text{for all real }x$$

In terms of discriminants, $q$ having none means its graph misses the horizontal axis, and substituting a line cannot pull it back down.

The composite has no real roots either.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The roots of the composite are the abscissas whose image under $f$ is a root of $q$, so they are the roots of $q$ pulled back through the line.

$$g(x)=0$$

$$f(x)\text{ is a root of }q$$

One concrete pair shows the shift at once.

$$f(x)=x+1$$

$$q(y)=y^{2}$$

$$g(x)$$

$$q(y)=(x+1)^{2}$$

The only root of $q$ is $0$, while the only root of $g$ is $-1$, so the two sets do not coincide.

The line moves the roots unless it happens to be the identity.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Falsch

The expansion already displays the Leitkoeffizient of the composite, and the slope of the line is squared into it.

$$g(x)=Am^{2}x^{2}+(2Amk+Bm)x+(Ak^{2}+Bk+C)$$

So the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $Am^{2}$, which equals $A$ only in the special case $m^{2}=1$.

$$m = 2$$

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{2}$$

$$g(x)= 4A\neq A\text{ unless }A$$

$$g(x)=0$$

Since $A\neq 0$ is assumed, a slope such as $m=2$ genuinely changes the number in front of $x^{2}$.

The Leitkoeffizient is $Am^{2}$, not $A$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.92.context: A non-constant line $f$ has slope $m$, and an outer parabola is written $q(y)=Ay^{2}+By+C$ with nonzero $A$. Set $g(x)=q(f(x))$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.92.solution_overview:
Nothing is numeric here, so the sign of the discriminant is the only lever available.

$$\Delta=b^{2}-4ac$$

Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird.

The parabola arrives as a second function wrapped around a line, so the substitution has to be unwound before the roots can be read.

MATH 7.93.title: Gleiche Werte und die Achse
statements: Die Gerade $\ell$ geht durch den Mittelpunkt von $u$ und $v$.
Die Zahlen $u$ und $v$ müssen die Wurzeln von $g$ sein.
Für jedes positive reelle $t$ tragen die beiden Punkte im Abstand $t$ von $\ell$ zu beiden Seiten gleiche Werte von $g$.
Die Summe $u+v$ ist allein durch die Koeffizienten von $g$ bestimmt.
Such a pair of distinct numbers with equal values exists for every quadratic $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Schreibe $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ mit $a\neq 0$. Two equal values give an equation between the coefficients, so subtract the two evaluations and factor.

$$g(u)-g(v)=a(u^{2}-v^{2})+b(u-v)$$

$$g(u)-g(v)=(u-v)\bigl(a(u+v)+b\bigr)$$

The first factor is non-zero because $u$ and $v$ are distinct, so the second one must vanish, which pins down the sum.

$$a(u+v)+b = 0$$

$$a(u+v)+b=\frac{u+v}{2}$$

$$g(u)-g(v)=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

The right-hand side is exactly the abscissa of the Symmetrieachse.

The axis passes through the midpoint of the two abscissas.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Equal values need not be zero values, so nothing forces the common value onto the horizontal axis.

$$g(x)=x^{2}$$

$$u=1$$

$$v=-1$$

$$g(1)=1$$

$$g(1)=g(-1)$$

The hypothesis is satisfied with a common value of $1$, yet the only root of this parabola is $0$, which is neither $u$ nor $v$.

$$g(x) = 0$$

$$x$$

$$g(1)=0$$

Symmetric pairs of abscissas exist at every height, not only at height zero.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

Vertex form makes the symmetry visible: only the distance from the axis enters, through a square.

$$g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$$

$$\ell:\ x=h$$

Evaluating at the two abscissas $h+t$ and $h-t$ squares the same number up to sign, so the two results agree.

$$g(h+t)=at^{2}+k$$

$$g(h-t)=at^{2}+k$$

This holds for every positive $t$, and the two abscissas are genuinely different because $t\neq 0$.

Points mirrored in the axis always carry the same value.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Write $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$. The relation derived from $g(u)=g(v)$ involved no data beyond the coefficients, so read it again.

$$(u-v)\bigl(a(u+v)+b\bigr)=0,\quad u\neq v$$

$$u+v=-\frac{b}{a}$$

Whatever pair of distinct abscissas with equal values one starts from, its sum is this one number, which is twice the abscissa of the axis.

The sum is fixed by $a$ and $b$ alone.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The Symmetrieachse always exists, and it supplies such a pair for free.

$$h=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

$$u=h+1$$

$$v=h-1$$

These two numbers are distinct, and Scheitelpunktform shows they carry the same value.

$$g(h+1)=a+k$$

$$g(h+1)=g(h-1)$$

The construction only needs $a\neq 0$, which is part of being a quadratic function, so it works for every $g$ of this kind.

Such a pair can always be produced.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.93.context: A parabola $g$ has nonzero Leitkoeffizient and Symmetrieachse $\ell$. Two distinct real numbers $u$ and $v$ satisfy $g(u)=g(v)$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.93.solution_overview:
Arithmetic is unavailable here: the coefficients stay symbolic, so the axis formula has to be argued with rather than evaluated.

$$x=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig.

The axis carries its own name here, and every letter compares it with some other line.

MATH 7.94.title: Ein Geradenbüschel und zwei Tangenten
statements: Jede Gerade der Schar geht durch ein und denselben Punkt.
Es gibt genau zwei Steigungen, für die die Gerade die Parabel in einem einzigen Punkt berührt.
Es gibt Steigungen, für die die Gerade die Parabel vollständig verfehlt.
For every slope the line meets the parabola at two distinct points.
Der feste Punkt, der allen Geraden gemeinsam ist, liegt auf der Parabel.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The parameter multiplies the bracket $x-1$, so it loses all its influence wherever that bracket vanishes.

$$f_{t}(1)=t\cdot 0+2$$

$$f_{t}(1)=2$$

Every member of the family therefore reaches the height $2$ at the abscissa $1$, whatever the slope.

$$t = 0$$

$$f_{0}(x)$$

$$f_{t}(1)=2$$

$$t=3$$

$$f_{3}(x)$$

$$t=3x-1$$

Both of these pass through $(1,2)$, and the same computation works for any slope: the family is a pencil of lines hinged at that point.

One fixed point is common to all the lines.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Touching at a single point means $g(x)=f_{t}(x)$ has a repeated solution, so collect the terms and set the discriminant to zero.

$$x^{2}-4x+6-t(x-1)-2=x^{2}-(4+t)x+(4+t)$$

$$x^{2}-4x+6-t(x-1)-2=0$$

$$\Delta(t)=(4+t)^{2}-4(4+t)$$

$$\Delta(t)=t(4+t)$$

The condition is now a quadratic equation in the slope, and it factors immediately.

$$t(4+t) = 0$$

$$t$$

$$\Delta(t)=0\text{ or }t$$

$$\Delta(t)=-4$$

The first gives the horizontal line $y=2$ touching at the vertex $(2,2)$, the second the line $y=-4x+6$ touching at $(0,6)$.

There are exactly two such slopes.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

A member misses the parabola exactly when the discriminant is negative, so study the sign of the product just obtained.

$$\Delta(t)=t(4+t)$$

A product of two factors is negative when they have opposite signs, which happens strictly between the two roots.

$$-4<t<0$$

$$\Delta(t)<0$$

$$t = -2$$

$$t=\Delta(-2)$$

$$\Delta(t)=(-2)\cdot 2$$

$$\Delta(t)=-4$$

$$-4<0$$

The line $y=-2x+4$ therefore shares no point with the curve.

Slopes in that window make the line miss the parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

Two distinct meetings need a strictly positive discriminant, and the discriminant has already been factored.

$$\Delta(t)=t(4+t)$$

It vanishes at $t=0$ and $t=-4$, where the line only touches the curve, and it is negative in between, where nothing is shared.

$$t = -2$$

$$\Delta$$

$$\Delta(t)=-4$$

$$-4<0$$

$$t=0$$

Some slopes give one meeting and some give none, so two distinct meetings do not always occur.

The claim fails for a whole interval of slopes.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Falsch

The fixed point of the pencil was found to be $(1,2)$, so test whether the parabola reaches that height there.

$$g(1)=1^{2}-4+6$$

$$1^{2}=1$$

$$g(1)=1-4+6$$

$$g(1)=1-4$$

$$g(1)=-3$$

$$g(1)=-3+6$$

$$g(1)=3$$

The parabola is at height $3$ while the fixed point sits at height $2$, so the point lies strictly below the curve.

$$\text{vertex of }g=(2,2),\qquad g(1)=3\neq 2$$

That position is exactly what makes the two tangent lines and the window of missing lines possible.

The hinge point of the family is not on the parabola.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.94.context: A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+6$ is compared with the family of lines $f_t(x)=t(x-1)+2$ obtained as the real parameter $t$ varies. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
MATH 7.94.solution_overview:
A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+6$ is compared with the family of lines $f_t(x)=t(x-1)+2$ obtained as the real parameter $t$ varies.

Rekonstruiere hier einmal die gemeinsame Gerade und Parabel; jeder Buchstabe prüft nur die in seiner Behauptung genannte Zusatzrechnung.

$g-f_t=x^{2}-(4+t)x+(4+t)$ with discriminant $t(4+t)$: two tangent slopes, and no meeting in between.

$$
f_{t}(1) = t\cdot 0+2 = 2
$$

$$
t = 0\implies f_{0}(x) = 2,\qquad t = 3\implies f_{3}(x) = 3x-1
$$

$$
x^{2}-4x+6-t(x-1)-2 = x^{2}-(4+t)x+(4+t) = 0
$$

MATH 7.95.title: Die Parabel seitlich verschieben
statements: Es gibt genau eine Verschiebung, für die die Gerade tangential an die Parabel ist.
Bei hinreichend negativen Verschiebungen treffen sich Gerade und Parabel nicht.
The vertex height of $g_r$ depends on $r$.
The Symmetrieachse of $g_r$ moves as $r$ changes.
Jede Parabel der Schar schneidet die $y$-Achse im selben Punkt.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The family moves a fixed parabola left and right, and tangency means $g_{r}(x)=f(x)$ has a repeated solution.

$$(x-r)^{2}-4-(2x-1)=x^{2}-(2r+2)x+(r^{2}-3)$$

$$(x-r)^{2}-4-(2x-1)=0$$

$$\Delta(r)=(2r+2)^{2}-4(r^{2}-3)$$

$$\Delta(r)=8r+16$$

The squares in $r$ cancel, so the condition is a first-degree equation with one solution.

$$8r+16 = 0$$

$$r$$

$$\Delta(r)=-2$$

At that shift the difference becomes $(x+1)^{2}$, a perfect square touching zero once.

Exactly one shift makes the line tangent.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Missing each other means a negative discriminant, and the discriminant just computed increases steadily with the shift.

$$\Delta(r)=8r+16$$

$$r<-2$$

$$\Delta(r)<0$$

Taking $r=-3$, for instance, leaves no real solution:

$$\Delta(r)=\Delta(-3)$$

$$\Delta(r)=-24+16$$

$$\Delta(r)=-8$$

$$-8<0$$

Pushed far enough to the left, the parabola has slid out from under the rising line and the two curves share nothing.

Sufficiently negative shifts separate the graphs.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

The formula is already in Scheitelpunktform, so the Extrempunkt can be read straight off it.

$$g_{r}(x) = (x-r)^{2}-4$$

$$\text{vertex}=(r,-4)$$

The shift appears in the bracket only, which moves the vertex sideways; the constant $-4$ outside the square is the height, and $r$ never enters it.

$$r = 0$$

$$\text{vertex }(0,-4)$$

$$r=5$$

$$\text{vertex }(5,-4)$$

The vertex height stays $-4$ for every shift.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The Symmetrieachse is the vertical line through the vertex, and Scheitelpunktform puts the vertex at abscissa $r$.

$$g_{r}(x) = (x-r)^{2}-4$$

$$\ell:\ x=r$$

The mirrored values confirm it, since only the distance from $r$ enters the square.

$$g_{r}(r+t)=t^{2}-4$$

$$g_{r}(r+t)=g_{r}(r-t)$$

Changing $r$ therefore drags the axis along with the whole graph.

The axis moves exactly as much as the shift.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The crossing with the vertical coordinate axis is the value at $x=0$, so substitute and see whether the shift survives.

$$g_{r}(0)=(0-r)^{2}-4$$

$$g_{r}(0)=r^{2}-4$$

The result depends on $r$, and two members already disagree.

$$r = 0$$

$$g_{0}(0)$$

$$g_{r}(0)=-4$$

$$r=3$$

$$g_{3}(0)$$

$$r=5$$
